generatedProse.concept-context: A psychology student planning a project sees the thread clearly. Their review of memory studies names a gap: one age group has rarely been tested. That gap becomes the proposal's question and shapes the method they choose. The report then answers the same question, so the whole project reads as one.
generatedProse.worked-example: A psychology student starts with a review of studies on sleep and memory and notices that students revising overnight have rarely been studied. The proposal turns that gap into a clear question and a simple method. The report presents the results plainly and saves their meaning for the discussion. Because each genre fed the next, the project answers the question the review first raised.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, the review, the proposal and the report carry one project between them. You can now connect the gap you find to the question you ask and the findings you report, rather than treating each document alone. One clear thread from review to report is what makes a psychology project hold together.

check.body: A student finds a gap in the literature, builds a proposal whose question targets that gap, carries out the study, and writes a report whose results answer the same question. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three genres worked as one connected project, each carrying the work of the one before it forward.
_items.feedback: Yes. One thread runs from the review's gap to the report's findings.

_items.text: That the student wrote more words than a project of this kind needs.
_items.feedback: Length is not the point; the connection between the genres is.

_items.text: That the literature review alone decided the whole project's success.
_items.feedback: The review started the thread, but the proposal and report carried it on.

_items.text: That the report could have been written before the proposal with no difference.
_items.feedback: The order matters: the report answers the question the proposal set.
